title: Weird performance
body:
Hi,
I tested Whisper.cpp on my laptop (Thinkpad T480s) with the small model. It executed the command in 7 seconds. I couldn't wait to get home to see how it would perform on my desktop.

I've just done it and it executes the same command in 14 seconds... This result surprised me. I looked on UserBenchmark for the performance of my 2 CPUs. The T480s uses an i5-8250U (4 cores 8 threads) and the PC a Ryzen 5 2600 (6 cores 12 threads). According to the site, the Ryzen is 40% more powerful, so I don't understand why it's slower on the PC than on the laptop.

In both cases, I compiled with these commands:
cmake -B build -D WHISPER_FFMPEG=yes
cmake --build build -j --config Release

and ran a test with this command:
time ./whisper-cli -m ./ggml-small.bin -f ./jfk.wav

## Thinkpad
OS: MX Linux (Ubuntu based)
RAM: 8 GB
CPU: i5-8250U
GPU: Intel UHD 620

## Desktop
OS: Ubuntu 24.04.2
RAM: 48 GB
CPU: Ryzen 5 2600
GPU: RX 5500 XT

Can somebody tell me if something is wrong with my desktop?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
The time command is not very helpful here. Run them again and pay attention to the whisper_print_timings numbers at the end. Pay particular attention to the time breakdown before the final runtime number as that shows where it's slowest/fastest.

Compare the system_info lines

e.g. (8250U)

> system_info: n_threads = 4 / 8 | WHISPER : COREML = 0 | OPENVINO = 1 | CPU : SSE3 = 1 | SSSE3 = 1 | AVX = 1 | AVX2 = 1 | F16C = 1 | FMA = 1 | BMI2 = 1 | OPENMP = 1 | AARCH64_REPACK = 1 |

Not got a Ryzen 5 2600 so not sure what that'll look like

To speed things up try compiling with Vulkan (as CUDA isn't available to you) - that should be fastest
For CPU-only try OpenVINO which is a lesser boost - no graphics driver needed...

Using budget GPU laptop I get the following timings (guide only as laptop's in front of me - using a cheap 11320H with GTX 1650)

CPU - 6.796 s
OpenVino - 2.938 s
Vulkan - 1.501 s

i.e. each improved one is roughly twice as fast (Vulkan depends highly on the GPU though)

For what it's worth cuda on the test lappy came in at 2.442 s under Windows. Oddly Windows is faster with Vulkan while Linux is faster with CUDA

Trying to run with longer text samples helps find out what's lacking too...

Yeah, using a GPU makes a big difference. AMD also have HIP but only on newer cards.

Just installed Ubuntu on the 1650 lappy to see what happens with older / smaller GPUs. On the older card Vulkan is also faster under linux than CUDA. This is reversed with newer cards tho (my 4070 is faster CUDA than Vulkan)

Also as the 1650 only has 4G VRAM it I just found out it crashes with large-v3 under Linux (I wondered what would happen). Need to go check what happens with Windows in a bit (may be different - as in slow but no crash - dunno yet)

Ooh - large-v3-turbo is OK though - 3.364 vulkan, 8.469 cuda (no tensor cores on 1650)

There are also the RPC backends and the whisper-server example - which should, hopefully, allow using both machines at once - yeah, gonna try that too...

An interesting experiment on your Desktop would be to disable the GPU in the BIOS so Linux is forced to use the CPU's IGPU (just tried that on the test laptop) - your laptop will also allow this...

Running cli will now use the IGPU, and be much slower, but how much slower is the interesting question (I got 3.5s for Vulkan small vs 1.5s for GPU) - I actually bought this test laptop to try SYCL out on so Intel 11th gen or better CPU was a must...
